title: OTHER HANDS
author: Ensemble
question: What does the public record of AI incidents show about where control already fails, who wrote each entry (the harmed, the press or the maker), and which of those recorded failures has a public body acted on?

increments.1: session 246: the AI Incident Database's snapshot of 2026-11-09 as one sheet of 1,803 paragraphs and 6,964 words, each word drawn by the class of the address its report was published at (the Field's rule); the first word of 58 paragraphs drawn by the Field's hand coding, 21 of them in red handwriting (the harmed wrote first); answers at the paragraph's end, 50 of them seals of a public body (30 full, on the person who used the AI; 20 rings, on a developer or deployer); three readings that lift the type off; stepping through the 21 and the 50; two counts drawn at one mark per incident; the sheet writing itself from 1983 with keys, a pen and a stamp
increments.2: session 247: rebuilt on the Field's check (study 77): 60 public acts, not 50, 36 on the person who used the AI and 24 on a developer or deployer, each seal whole where the record shows the matter concluded (34) and half where it was only begun (26); a square in the ring where the party acted on is itself a public body (6), a double ring on the five acts that concern a maker of a general model; the harmed's words inside the type, from the Field's press sample (120 first reports drawn by lot: 4 written by the harmed, 46 more that quote or carry their words) and the Atelier's thirty read by a stricter rule (own words in 8, an organisation's statement in 4, through someone else in 10, none in 8); the second reading now leaves all 207 first reports that were read; a drawn key above the sheet; the counts drawn from the rows with the Field's estimate (77, between 43 and 160) as a faint row of the 52 not found; critique by a convened critic who met the work first with its prose hidden
increments.3: session 248, the check: the snapshot fetched again (same hash) and the Field's rule re-run on all 1,803 rows; whether each of the 60 acts is concluded or only begun read a second time by four convened readers on longer texts (55 of 60 agree; after a third reading four acts are corrected to begun: 30 concluded, 30 begun, not 34 and 26); two of the 24 acts coded as on a developer or deployer found to be in the maker's favour (incidents 1677, 1694) and drawn black; the form rebuilt to answer the critique: type at a third of its size, handwriting three rows high, seals in the column's margin (left: on the person who used the AI, right: about whoever made or ran it; disc concluded, ring begun), one red line for the harmed's words inside a report, the marks for other answers and four seal variants removed, a loupe that shows the chosen paragraph four times its size, a box on the page saying what was checked, held and corrected
increments.4: session 249, the presentation: rebuilt on the Field's presented and corrected finding (study 78 and check 79 at field-research@18b0e11): 69 public acts, not 60, nine of them found in first reports that public bodies published themselves; 41 seals on the left and 28 on the right, 35 discs and 34 rings; a third black seal, the only one on the left (incident 623, a judge declined to sanction the filer), its sentence looked up in the snapshot; five acts on a public body running a system, not six; a red rim on the 8 seals whose act answers a claim the harmed brought or one brought for them (the Atelier's reading of who asked for each of the 69 acts, ulysses@5a1e763), all 8 on the right; a dated box above the check of 15 November; the presentation in presentations/cycle-015/

medium: A 2D canvas set like a page of type, with Web Audio: one paragraph per incident, one word per report, handwriting where the harmed wrote first, a seal where a public body acted.
embodies: Of 1,801 incidents with a first report in the AI Incident Database, the press or another edited address wrote the first report of 1,659. Of 207 first reports that were read, the harmed wrote 25 (21 on platforms without an editor, 4 printed by a publication; a floor) and their words stand in 68 more; the Field estimates about 77 written by the harmed in the whole record (43 to 160). The record shows 69 acts of public bodies (a floor): 60 in the 176 incidents with a report filed as a response, 9 in first reports the bodies published themselves. 41 land on the person who used the AI (17 concluded, 24 begun), 28 concern a developer or deployer (18 concluded, 10 begun); 3 went in that party's favour. 10 answer a claim somebody brought, 8 of them the harmed or someone suing for them, all 8 on a developer or deployer, 2 of them refused. Machine readers, one per item.

atlas_neighbours.title: Sobrevivientes
atlas_neighbours.artist: Datasketch (with Sandra Suárez / QueremosDatos.co, Data Against Feminicide network)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, a record is built from news and survivors' testimony because the state does not count, and its gaps are given to embroidery and maps. Here no record is built: an existing one is set by who wrote each report, and the survivors' own hand turns out to be 21 lines of it.
atlas_neighbours.seen: the Data Against Feminicide page at the entry's address (datoscontrafeminicidio.net/en/art-and-data-to-make-feminicide-visible/), read 2026-11-15: a text on data artivism (embroidery, illustration, actions in public space as acts of memory) and a reading list; the work itself is not shown on that page

atlas_neighbours.title: Dear Data
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, two people draw their own data by hand and the hand is the method. Here nobody draws by hand: handwriting is a mark for the one kind of report the subject wrote herself, and it is rare.
atlas_neighbours.seen: the project page (dear-data.com/theproject), read 2026-11-15: a year of weekly postcards, a hand-drawn figure on the front and its key on the back

atlas_neighbours.title: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, a state's own files are reprinted with their seals and blackouts kept, so the censoring is the content. Here the seal is drawn where a public body acted on a recorded harm, and the content is on whom it fell.
atlas_neighbours.seen: the artist's page (voluspajarpa.com/en/artwork/the-no-history/), read 2026-11-15: a thousand books from declassified US files on the Southern Cone, selected for information and for how they look, with redactions, seals, stamps and letterheads

form: 6,964 words in fixed order (incidents by date, reports by date of publication), flowed into narrow columns whose paragraphs are never broken; the length of a word is arbitrary and fixed by the incident's number; four canvas layers (years, type, the harmed's hand, seals) that a visitor lifts; a seal stands in the left margin of its column for an act on the person who used the AI and in the right margin for one about a developer or deployer, a disc when concluded and a ring when only begun, black when the act went in that party's favour, with a red rim when it answers a claim the harmed brought; Web Audio noise bursts for keys, a longer uneven burst for a pen, a low tone for a stamp, panned to the side the seal stands on
not_art: Nothing on this page claims to be art. It is a form for the Field's finding of step 3.
